data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) suspension and debarment (S/D) guidance for nonprocurement and procurement programs and activities.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) suspension and debarment (S/D) guidance for nonprocurement and procurement programs and activities

policy_statements.source_text: It complies with Title 2 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 180, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Guidelines to Agencies on Governmentwide Debarment and Suspension (Nonprocurement), adopted and supplemented by USDA at 2 CFR Part 417, Nonprocurement Debarment and Suspension, and with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 9.4, codified at 48 CFR Subpart 9.4, Debarment, Suspension, and Ineligibility, adopted and supplemented by USDA at 48 CFR Subpart 409.4, Debarment, Suspension and Ineligibility (hereinafter FAR and Agriculture Acquisition Regulation (AGAR) respectively).
cross_references: Title 2 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 180, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Guidelines to Agencies on Governmentwide Debarment and Suspension (Nonprocurement)
2 CFR Part 417, Nonprocurement Debarment and Suspension
48 CFR Subpart 9.4, Debarment, Suspension, and Ineligibility
48 CFR Subpart 409.4, Debarment, Suspension and Ineligibility

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for or on behalf of USDA.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for or on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This directive supersedes DR 2280-001, Suspension and Debarment, dated January 16, 2013.
cross_references: DR 2280-001, Suspension and Debarment, dated January 16, 2013

policy_statements.source_text: This directive becomes effective as of the publication date and remains in effect until it is superseded or it expires.
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their S/D policies and guidance with this directive upon its publication.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will implement S/D actions in accordance with the applicable nonprocurement or procurement regulations and with the procedures set forth in this DR to ensure that:
Only presently responsible persons participate in USDA programs; and
USDA only solicits offers from, awards contracts to, and consents to subcontracts with presently responsible entities.

Suspensions and debarments are discretionary or statutory administrative actions taken by Federal agencies to protect the Government by excluding individuals and entities who are not presently responsible from participating in Federal programs or activities.
These actions are not designed to be punitive in nature but are meant to ensure that the Federal Government only conducts business with presently responsible individuals or entities.
S/D actions are reciprocal and thus applicable Governmentwide.
Consequently, an individual or entity suspended or debarred by one Federal agency is excluded from entering into procurement and covered nonprocurement transactions with all Federal agencies.
The Secretary has established an S/D Council (“the Council”) to coordinate USDA efforts to ensure effective implementation of S/D procedures.
The Council will meet quarterly, or as appropriate, to develop strategies and initiatives to effectively implement USDA’s S/D program.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to report to the Council on their respective S/D activity.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA’s Office of the Chief Financial Officer’s (OCFO) Transparency and Accountability Reporting Division (TARD) will capture a summarized S/D activity report on an OCFO restricted access intranet site, currently a restricted access OCFO information repository.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA’s Office of the Chief Financial Officer’s (OCFO) Transparency and Accountability Reporting Division (TARD)

policy_statements.source_text: Executive Order (EO) 12549, Debarment and Suspension, mandates that Executive Departments and Agencies establish appropriate procedures to implement 2 CFR Part 180.
USDA’s nonprocurement S/D regulations are promulgated in 2 CFR Part 417.
FAR 9.402(e) mandates that Federal agencies establish appropriate procedures to implement FAR Subpart 9.4.
USDA’s procurement S/D regulations are promulgated in the AGAR at 48 CFR Subpart 409.4.

Pursuant to EO 12689, Debarment and Suspension, the suspension, debarment, or other exclusion of a participant in a nonprocurement program or activity under regulations issued under EO 12549, or in a procurement program or activity under regulations issued under FAR Subpart 9.4, will have reciprocal Governmentwide effect.

That is, a person or entity that is suspended or debarred from nonprocurement programs or activities is also excluded from procurement programs or activities, and vice versa, across the Federal Government.
Nonprocurement causes for suspension and debarment are listed in the following sections:
2 CFR § 180.700, When may the suspending official issue a suspension;
cross_references: 2 CFR § 180.700, When may the suspending official issue a suspension

policy_statements.source_text: 2 CFR § 180.800, What are the causes for debarment;
cross_references: 2 CFR § 180.800, What are the causes for debarment

policy_statements.source_text: and 2 CFR § 417.800, What are the USDA causes for debarment.
cross_references: 2 CFR § 417.800, What are the USDA causes for debarment

policy_statements.source_text: Procurement causes for suspension and debarment are listed in FAR 9.407-2 and FAR 9.406-2 respectively.
In addition to the causes for regulatory nonprocurement and procurement S/D actions discussed above, there are several statutory debarment provisions.
S/D actions undertaken pursuant to these provisions are not reciprocal across the Federal Government.
For reciprocity to occur, an agency must also undertake a regulatory nonprocurement or procurement suspension or debarment action in conjunction with the statutory suspension or debarment action.
policy_statements.target: regulatory nonprocurement or procurement suspension or debarment action

policy_statements.source_text: Section 14211 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008, Public Law (P.L.) 110-246; 7 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 2209j; 2 CFR § 417.865(d), requires the Secretary to “permanently debar an individual, organization, corporation, or other entity convicted of a felony for knowingly defrauding the United States in connection with any program administered by the Department of Agriculture from any subsequent participation in Department of Agriculture programs” – both procurement and nonprocurement.
cross_references: Section 14211 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008, Public Law (P.L.) 110-246

policy_statements.source_text: Those debarred pursuant to this statutory provision are permanently excluded from participating in all USDA procurement and nonprocurement programs or activities, even those normally considered not covered transactions, with the only exception being that continued participation in domestic food assistance programs is allowed for those permanently debarred.
conditions: with the only exception being that continued participation in domestic food assistance programs is allowed for those permanently debarred

policy_statements.source_text: A list of domestic food assistance programs is set forth in 2 CFR § 417.865(d)(2).
Unlike regulatory S/D actions which are discretionary, S/D actions under this statute are mandatory.

16 U.S.C. § 620d(d) provides that any person who violates 16 U.S.C. §§ 620-620j, or any regulation or contract issued under 16 U.S.C. §§ 620-620j, may be debarred from entering into any contract for the purchase of unprocessed timber from Federal lands for a period of not more than 5 years.
Such person shall also be precluded from taking delivery of Federal timber purchased by another party for the period of debarment.

7 U.S.C. § 2021(h) provides that the Department can immediately suspend a retail food store or wholesale food concern in the event of flagrant violations of the Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program.
This suspension may be taken before an administrative action to disqualify.

The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020, P.L. 116-93, §§ 744 and 745 (December 20, 2019), as amended or as amended and subsequently enacted, is a mandatory statutory debarment provision included in annual appropriations acts.

It prohibits using funds made available by any act to enter into contracts, memoranda of understanding, or cooperative agreements with, make grants to, or provide loans or loan guarantees to corporations that have been convicted of a felony within the preceding 24 months or have a fully adjudicated and remaining unpaid tax delinquency, unless a Federal agency considered suspension or debarment and determined that such action was not necessary to protect the interests of the Government.
conditions: unless a Federal agency considered suspension or debarment and determined that such action was not necessary to protect the interests of the Government

policy_statements.source_text: When considering S/D actions, the S/D Official (SDO) must refer to the appropriations legislation in the year that corresponds to the proposed S/D action.
policy_statements.target: appropriations legislation in the year that corresponds to the proposed S/D action

policy_statements.source_text: S/D actions can be taken against individuals with respect to nonprocurement transactions under a USDA program even if such action has been excluded from covered transaction status.
conditions: even if such action has been excluded from covered transaction status

policy_statements.source_text: Evidence of the existence of a potential cause for a nonprocurement or procurement suspension or debarment action may be discovered through sources including, but not limited to, the USDA Office of the Inspector General (OIG) or the Department of Justice (DOJ) investigations; civil or criminal court actions; hotline complaints; media reports; recommendations of the USDA Departmental Scientific Integrity Officer (DSIO) or Research Integrity Officer (RIO); USDA records and reviews of individuals or entities participating in USDA procurement and nonprocurement programs or activities; and records or reports from other Federal agencies.

It should also be noted that while the quarterly OIG report and OIG investigations can be helpful tools to reveal potential causes for S/D actions, not all information contained in the OIG quarterly report nor every OIG investigation results in a potential cause for S/D actions.
Whenever information about a potential cause for suspension or debarment becomes known, the concerned Mission Area, agency or staff office S/D personnel will conduct its own review.
policy_statements.actor_name: concerned Mission Area, agency or staff office S/D personnel
conditions: Whenever information about a potential cause for suspension or debarment becomes known

policy_statements.source_text: The concerned Mission Area, agency, or staff office may request OIG assistance when warranted.
policy_statements.actor_name: concerned Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: (See DR 1700-002, OIG Organization and Procedures, Section 8c.)
cross_references: DR 1700-002, OIG Organization and Procedures, Section 8c.

policy_statements.source_text: Nonprocurement Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel will forward the results of the inquiry to the Program Manager.
policy_statements.actor_name: Nonprocurement Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Procurement Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel will forward the results of the inquiry to the Contracting Officer.
policy_statements.actor_name: Procurement Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: The Program Manager or Contracting Officer in collaboration with S/D Council Members, and with the Office of the General Counsel (OGC) when needed, will determine whether information obtained during the inquiry should be forwarded to the SDO for possible suspension or debarment action.

If forwarding is appropriate, the Program Manager or Contracting Officer in collaboration with a S/D Council Member, will prepare the Referral Record and Referral Record Memorandum and submit it to the SDO for a decision.
policy_statements.target: Referral Record and Referral Record Memorandum

policy_statements.source_text: The Referral Record is used to establish the Administrative Record if the SDO determines that suspension or debarment is warranted.
conditions: if the SDO determines that suspension or debarment is warranted

policy_statements.source_text: (See Appendix E, Template: Nonprocurement Referral Record and Referral Record Memorandum and Appendix G, Template: Procurement Referral Record and Referral Record Memorandum.)
The Referral Memorandum will address potential causes for S/D actions.
This memorandum should summarize the history and background of the proposed action, state the period of suspension or debarment, and include supporting documentation.
The memorandum may precede other recommendations such as show cause or pre-notice investigative letters.
The purpose of lead agency coordination is to coordinate Governmentwide suspension and debarment actions across one or more Federal agencies.
(See Section 6c(2) below.)
The Program Manager informs the nonprocurement S/D Coordinator, or the Contracting Officer informs the procurement S/D Coordinator, of a potential suspension or debarment action.

The nonprocurement S/D Coordinator forwards excluded individual or entity identifying information; the reason for the proposed action; a due date when other USDA and Federal agencies can respond to the notice; and the Mission Area, agency, or staff office point(s) of contact concerning the action to the OCFO for lead agency coordination.
Similarly, the procurement S/D Coordinator forwards the information to the Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP).

The OCFO and the OCP coordinate with other Federal agencies through the Interagency Suspension and Debarment Committee (ISDC) to facilitate the sharing of suspension or debarment information and to prevent duplicative efforts should another Federal agency express an interest in or initiate an action against the same individual or entity.
USDA and other interested Federal agencies will decide on the lead agency that will initiate and take responsibility for the suspension or debarment action.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA and other interested Federal agencies

policy_statements.source_text: In general, if more than one USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office has an interest, lead agency may be designated by the Mission Area, agency, or staff office with the largest interest and/or award value with the individual(s) or entity(ies).
conditions: if more than one USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office has an interest

policy_statements.source_text: If the lead is assigned to the USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office, the S/D Coordinator will coordinate with USDA stakeholders and with other interested Federal agencies and offices to share and obtain information and developments relevant to the action.
policy_statements.target: USDA stakeholders and with other interested Federal agencies and offices
conditions: If the lead is assigned to the USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: The lead agency, or the lead USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office, acts on behalf of all Federal agencies and has a responsibility to keep other interested Federal agencies informed of significant developments.
policy_statements.actor_name: lead agency, or the lead USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: The other interested Federal agencies, in turn, may assist the lead agency by providing relevant information to enable the lead agency to effectively carry out its function.

If the lead agency coordination notice does not generate a response from another Federal agency seeking lead (after 7 calendar days of review), or if the lead is assigned to the initiating USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office, the Program Manager or Contracting Officer will prepare the Referral Record and Referral Record Memorandum used to establish an Administrative Record (see Appendices E and G) in consultation with OGC, when needed.
policy_statements.target: Referral Record and Referral Record Memorandum
conditions: If the lead agency coordination notice does not generate a response from another Federal agency seeking lead (after 7 calendar days of review), or if the lead is assigned to the initiating USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: The Program Manager or Contracting Officer will forward the Referral Record to either the nonprocurement or procurement S/D Council Member and S/D Coordinator, as appropriate.
The nonprocurement S/D Council Member consults with the OGC (for legal sufficiency) and the OIG (to ensure that the Referral Record will not interfere with any OIG investigative action).
The Council Member sends the Referral Record to nonprocurement S/D personnel for review who assigns a case number unique to each respondent referenced in the Referral Record.
This Referral Record may be used to establish an Administrative Record to be sent to the nonprocurement SDO for consideration.
The SDO follows the procedures set forth in both 2 CFR Parts 180 and 417, Subparts G and H, in deciding, initiating, and finalizing the S/D exclusion action.
cross_references: 2 CFR Parts 180 and 417, Subparts G and H

policy_statements.source_text: The procurement S/D Council Member consults with OGC (for legal sufficiency) and OIG (to ensure that the Referral Record will not interfere with any OIG investigative action).
The Council Member sends the Referral Record to OCP S/D personnel for review who assigns a case number unique to each respondent referenced in the Referral Record.
This Referral Record may be used to establish an Administrative Record to be sent to the procurement SDO for consideration.
The SDO follows the procedures set forth in FAR Subpart 9.4 and AGAR Subpart 409.4 in deciding, initiating, and finalizing the S/D exclusion action.

USDA adopted OMB guidelines for nonprocurement suspension and debarment which includes 2 CFR § 180.45 Do these guidelines cover persons who are disqualified, as well as those who are excluded from nonprocurement transactions and 2 CFR Part 180, Subpart E, System for Award Management Exclusions.
cross_references: 2 CFR § 180.45 Do these guidelines cover persons who are disqualified, as well as those who are excluded from nonprocurement transactions
2 CFR Part 180, Subpart E, System for Award Management Exclusions

policy_statements.source_text: These sections state that in addition to the discretionary actions included in this Governmentwide system, agencies may add disqualified persons to the General Services Administration’s (GSA) System for Award Management (SAM) Exclusions for disqualifications required by statute, executive order, or regulation.

Because of USDA’s adoption of 2 CFR Part 180, USDA disqualification actions may be included in GSA’s SAM Exclusions database as exclusion type Prohibition/Restriction, with a narrow explanation as to the scope of the prohibition or restriction and in accordance with Mission Area, agency, or staff office procedures.
It is up to each Mission Area, agency, or staff office to promulgate regulations for the inclusion of program-specific disqualifications in SAM.
policy_statements.actor_name: each Mission Area, agency, or staff office
policy_statements.target: regulations for the inclusion of program-specific disqualifications in SAM

policy_statements.source_text: Disqualifications do not have a Governmentwide or Departmentwide effect.
Disqualification actions will be reported to the OCFO in the Mission Area, agency, or staff office’s quarterly nonprocurement S/D report.
The following roles and responsibilities are applicable to both nonprocurement and procurement S/D actions.
The General Counsel will:
Provide legal advice, when requested, to the Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel, Program Managers, Contracting Officers, S/D Council Members, S/D Coordinators, and SDOs;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel, Program Managers, Contracting Officers, S/D Council Members, S/D Coordinators, and SDOs

policy_statements.source_text: Review proposed suspension or debarment or other exclusion action materials (e.g., Referral Records, Referral Memoranda, Decision Memoranda, Administrative Records) for legal sufficiency and inform SDOs of any legal risks; and
policy_statements.target: proposed suspension or debarment or other exclusion action materials (e.g., Referral Records, Referral Memoranda, Decision Memoranda, Administrative Records)

policy_statements.source_text: Assist the OIG, as necessary, with facilitating contact and coordination with the DOJ, the Assistant United States Attorney, or local prosecutors who may be handling a criminal or civil suit involving an individual or entity that is being considered for exclusion.
Primary coordination is typically provided by the OIG.
The Inspector General will:
Provide information to the Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices about actions of individuals and entities that may form the basis for S/D actions.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: OIG components, including the Office of Investigations and the Office of Audits, will conduct work which generates information sometimes suitable for S/D referrals.
policy_statements.actor_name: OIG components, including the Office of Investigations and the Office of Audits

policy_statements.source_text: Provide a quarterly report to the OCFO containing updated information on OIG investigations and indictments (and other charging mechanisms comparable to indictments), convictions, and pre-trial diversions.

Facilitate contact and coordination with the DOJ, the Assistant United States Attorney, or local prosecutors who may be handling a criminal or civil suit involving an individual or entity that is being considered for suspension, debarment, or other exclusion.
policy_statements.target: DOJ, the Assistant United States Attorney, or local prosecutors

policy_statements.source_text: If an action would interfere with an ongoing investigation, the OIG will consider requesting that the Department defer the action or seek special protections against disclosure of sensitive information.
conditions: If an action would interfere with an ongoing investigation

policy_statements.source_text: Remain involved in the S/D process until the case is resolved.
OIG personnel, when needed, will attend S/D meetings and hearings, provide testimony and other information and evidence regarding their work, and generally assist the S/D personnel.
The following roles and responsibilities are applicable to nonprocurement S/D actions.
Mission Area Agency Administrators and Staff Office Directors will:
Serve as SDOs;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Agency Administrators and Staff Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Determine if a suspension or debarment action is warranted based on the Administrative Record;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Agency Administrators and Staff Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Initiate suspension or debarment actions when warranted, taking into consideration consultations with the OGC, OIG, or DOJ regarding possible conflicts with ongoing civil or criminal investigations or litigation;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Agency Administrators and Staff Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Impose suspension or debarment actions in accordance with the procedures set forth in 2 CFR Parts 180 and 417;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Agency Administrators and Staff Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that S/D Coordinators, Program Managers, and all other designated Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel complete the S/D training available in AgLearn.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Agency Administrators and Staff Office Directors
policy_statements.target: S/D Coordinators, Program Managers, and all other designated Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: A certificate of completion (see Appendix H, Template: Mission Area, Agency, Staff Office S/D Training Certificate of Completion) must be provided to the OCFO by December 30 of each year.
This training requirement is optional if completed in prior calendar years.
conditions: if completed in prior calendar years

policy_statements.source_text: However, adherence to applicable updates must occur;
Establish S/D guidance or instructions that implement the Department’s policies and procedures and provide such guidance or instructions to the OCFO when established or modified.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Agency Administrators and Staff Office Directors
policy_statements.target: S/D guidance or instructions that implement the Department’s policies and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: The guidance or instructions should include, but not be limited to:
Controls and procedures to identify fraud and misconduct related to the Mission Area, agency, and staff office programs or activities;
An internal review plan for identifying cases to be referred for suspension or debarment actions; and
A training plan that:
Identifies all Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel required to take S/D training; and
Ensures all designated personnel are made aware of and follow procedures pursuant to the Governmentwide S/D regulations and the Department’s S/D directive(s).
The Chief Financial Officer’s Director of the TARD will:

Receive OIG quarterly reports containing updated information on OIG investigations and indictments (and other charging mechanisms comparable to indictments), convictions, and pre-trial diversions, and distribute to nonprocurement and procurement S/D Coordinators;
policy_statements.actor_name: Chief Financial Officer’s Director of the TARD
policy_statements.target: OIG quarterly reports containing updated information on OIG investigations and indictments (and other charging mechanisms comparable to indictments), convictions, and pre-trial diversions

policy_statements.source_text: Receive the Nonprocurement SAM Memorandum (Appendix D, Template: Nonprocurement SAM Memorandum) from nonprocurement S/D Coordinators and enter S/D exclusions in the GSA SAM Exclusions database;
policy_statements.actor_name: Chief Financial Officer’s Director of the TARD
policy_statements.target: Nonprocurement SAM Memorandum (Appendix D, Template: Nonprocurement SAM Memorandum)

policy_statements.source_text: Receive outside party inquiries regarding individual or entity status in the GSA SAM Exclusions database and refer the outside party to the requisite Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D Council Member or S/D Coordinator.
policy_statements.actor_name: Chief Financial Officer’s Director of the TARD
policy_statements.target: outside party inquiries regarding individual or entity status in the GSA SAM Exclusions database

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, agency, or staff office representatives delivering such responses should coordinate with the OGC as needed, to ensure that no deliberative process, attorney-client, privacy protected information, or attorney work product privileges are waived by sharing information with the outside party.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office representatives

policy_statements.source_text: Preventive measures must also be exercised to avoid improper disclosure of personally identifiable information as defined by the Privacy Act and related statutes.

Coordinate nonprocurement S/D issues within USDA and with other Federal agencies, including updating and maintaining USDA’s supplemental nonprocurement S/D regulation in 2 CFR Part 417 in collaboration with the OGC; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Chief Financial Officer’s Director of the TARD

policy_statements.source_text: Act as USDA’s nonprocurement point of contact (POC) for internal and external lead agency coordination.
policy_statements.actor_name: Chief Financial Officer’s Director of the TARD

policy_statements.source_text: The OCFO will notify Federal and USDA Mission Area, agencies, and staff offices of pending suspension or debarment actions and coordinate responses with the ISDC.
policy_statements.target: Federal and USDA Mission Area, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Council Members will:

Promote the requirements and purpose of the Governmentwide S/D regulations and direct their respective Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices to reevaluate S/D processes, as necessary, to support efficient stewardship of Federal funds.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Council Members
policy_statements.target: requirements and purpose of the Governmentwide S/D regulations

policy_statements.source_text: Council Members will ensure that Departmental guidance to implement Governmentwide and USDA S/D regulations are met and will report Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D activity at quarterly meetings held by the OCFO; and
policy_statements.target: Departmental guidance to implement Governmentwide and USDA S/D regulations

policy_statements.source_text: Send referrals to Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel who assigns a case number unique to each respondent, to create a Referral Record that may be used to establish an Administrative Record (if applicable) to be sent to the SDO for consideration, following consultation with the OGC (for its legal sufficiency) or the OIG (to ensure that the Referral Record will not interfere with any OIG investigative action) as appropriate.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Council Members
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: (See Section 6e.)
Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators will:
Receive exclusion information from Program Managers in collaboration with S/D Council Members and forward to the OCFO for lead agency coordination when applicable;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: Receive and review OIG’s quarterly report on the password protected S/D restricted access information repository maintained by OCFO which contains updated information on OIG investigations and indictments (and other charging mechanisms comparable to indictments), convictions, and pre-trial diversions, prepare applicable summaries and report to requisite Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D Council Members, Program Managers and other designated Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: Report fact-based S/D activity on the S/D restricted access information repository maintained by the OCFO, prepare applicable summaries, and report to requisite Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D Council Members, Program Managers and other designated Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: Share information and developments within USDA and other interested Federal agencies, as necessary, if lead agency coordination is assigned to the S/D Coordinator’s Mission Area, agency, or staff office;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators
conditions: if lead agency coordination is assigned to the S/D Coordinator’s Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Receive S/D information from the ISDC through the OCFO and distribute to Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D Council Members, Program Managers, and other designated S/D personnel for lead agency coordination;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D Council Members, Program Managers, and other designated S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Review Referral Records, in collaboration with S/D Council Members, to establish applicable Administrative Records received from S/D Council Members and Program Managers, assign a Mission Area, agency, or staff office case number unique to each respondent, and forward, where appropriate, to the SDO for consideration;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: Send the Nonprocurement SAM Memorandum (see Appendix D) to the OCFO accompanied by the Notice of Suspension, Debarment, Disqualification or Voluntary Exclusion signed by the SDO.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: The SAM Memorandum should be sent to the OCFO after respondent(s) notification(s) about suspension, debarment, and disqualification decisions, or following the receipt of an administrative agreement or settlement agreement between the respondent and the SDO that includes a voluntary exclusion (See 2 CFR §§ 180.715, 180.805, 180.935, 417.935, 180.1020, 417.520, and 417.515);
Provide the OCFO with the nonprocurement S/D report within 45 calendar days after a fiscal year (FY) quarter.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators
conditions: within 45 calendar days after a fiscal year (FY) quarter

policy_statements.source_text: S/D Council Members will use this information to brief the Council on Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D activity during quarterly S/D meetings held by the OCFO; and
Be the POC for outside party inquiries (e.g., banks, employers, or the general public) regarding individual or entity status in the GSA SAM Exclusions database.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: This includes verifying an identity match between the Mission Area, agency, or staff office excluded individuals or entities and the subject of the inquiry by the outside party.

As needed, coordinate with the OGC when responding to outside inquiries to ensure that no deliberative process, attorney-client, or attorney work product privileges are waived by sharing information with the outside party.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: Preventive measures must also be exercised to avoid improper disclosure of personally identifiable information as defined by the Privacy Act and related statutes.
Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Program Managers, in collaboration with S/D Council Members (or other designated program personnel) will:

Ensure that the requirements in 2 CFR § 180.425 are met, and that the GSA SAM Exclusions database is checked when required to confirm that only presently responsible individuals or entities can participate in USDA nonprocurement covered transactions;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Program Managers

policy_statements.source_text: Refer program violators, where appropriate, in any USDA program, to the S/D Coordinator for lead agency coordination, after confirming the existence of a possible cause for an exclusion action; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Program Managers
conditions: after confirming the existence of a possible cause for an exclusion action

policy_statements.source_text: Prepare the Nonprocurement Referral Record and Referral Memorandum in collaboration with an S/D Coordinator (see Appendix E, Template: Nonprocurement Referral Record and Referral Record Memorandum), and in consultation with the OIG and the OGC, if needed, to establish an Administrative Record, if applicable, and forward to the S/D Council Member when recommending the initiation of an exclusion action to a SDO.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Program Managers
policy_statements.target: Nonprocurement Referral Record and Referral Memorandum

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office S/D Personnel will:

In coordination with the OIG, where applicable, review and confirm potential causes for suspension or debarment actions obtained from external sources (e.g., OIG, other Federal agencies, hotline complaints, media) or through internal program operations (e.g., review of program participants and/or recipients), and report findings to their S/D Council Member and Program Manager; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office S/D Personnel
policy_statements.target: potential causes for suspension or debarment actions

policy_statements.source_text: Assist the S/D Council Member and Program Manager in any S/D-related program issues.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office S/D Personnel
policy_statements.target: S/D Council Member and Program Manager

policy_statements.source_text: The following roles and responsibilities are applicable to procurement S/D actions:
The OCP S/D Senior Procurement Official will:
Receive Administrative Records from the OCP staff and determine whether a suspension or debarment action is in the Government’s interest;

Initiate suspension or debarment actions when warranted, taking into consideration any advice received from the OGC, OIG, or DOJ regarding possible conflicts with ongoing civil or criminal investigations or litigation;
Impose suspension or debarment actions in accordance with the procedures set forth in FAR Subpart 9.4 and AGAR Subpart 409.4; and
Ensure that all contracting officers and procurement S/D personnel complete the S/D training available in AgLearn.
policy_statements.target: contracting officers and procurement S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: A certificate of completion (see Appendix H) will be provided to the OCFO by December 30 of each calendar year.
conditions: by December 30 of each calendar year

policy_statements.source_text: This training requirement is optional if completed in prior calendar years.
conditions: if completed in prior calendar years

policy_statements.source_text: However, adherence to applicable updates must occur.
The OCP Senior Procurement Official will:

Review the Referral Records received from the S/D Coordinators, assign a Mission Area, agency, or staff office case number unique to each respondent, and forward applicable Administrative Records to the SDO for consideration;
policy_statements.target: Referral Records received from the S/D Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: Enter Show Cause/Pre-notice investigative letter language;
Enter suspended or debarred contractors’ information in the GSA SAM Exclusions database;
Respond to outside party inquiries regarding a contractor’s status in the GSA SAM Exclusions database.
policy_statements.target: outside party inquiries regarding a contractor’s status in the GSA SAM Exclusions database

policy_statements.source_text: As needed, coordinate with the OGC when responding to outside inquiries to ensure that no deliberative process, attorney-client, privacy protected information, or attorney work product privileges are waived by sharing information with the outside party;
Coordinate procurement S/D issues within USDA and with other Federal agencies.
This includes updating and maintaining USDA’s supplemental procurement S/D regulation in AGAR Subpart 409.4;
Act as USDA’s procurement POC for lead agency coordination; and
Submit quarterly reports to the OCFO detailing the Department’s procurement S/D activity 45 calendar days after the FY quarter.
conditions: 45 calendar days after the FY quarter

policy_statements.source_text: The OCP’s S/D Council Member will:

Promote the requirements and purpose of the Governmentwide S/D regulations and direct their respective Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices to reevaluate S/D processes, as necessary, to support efficient stewardship of Federal funds.
policy_statements.target: requirements and purpose of the Governmentwide S/D regulations

policy_statements.source_text: Council Members will ensure that Departmental guidance to implement Governmentwide and USDA S/D regulations are met and will report Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D activity at quarterly meetings held by the OCFO; and
policy_statements.target: Departmental guidance to implement Governmentwide and USDA S/D regulations

policy_statements.source_text: Send referrals to Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel who assigns an agency case number unique to each respondent to create a Referral Record and Referral Memorandum.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: The Referral Record and Referral Memorandum may be used to establish an Administrative Record (if applicable) for submission to the SDO for consideration, following consultation with the OGC (for its legal sufficiency) or the OIG (to ensure that the Referral Record will not interfere with any OIG investigative action) as appropriate.
(See Section 6e.)
Mission Area Senior Contractor Officials will:
Receive suspension or debarment information from contracting officers and forward to the OCP for lead agency coordination;

Receive OIG’s quarterly report containing updated information on OIG investigations and indictments (and other charging mechanisms comparable to indictments), convictions, and pre-trial diversions from the OCFO and disseminate to all contracting officers and appropriate agency S/D personnel;
Review Referral Records received from contracting officers and forward to the OCP;
policy_statements.target: Referral Records received from contracting officers

policy_statements.source_text: Share information and developments within USDA and other interested Federal agencies, as necessary, if lead agency coordination is assigned to the S/D Coordinator’s Mission Area, agency, or staff office;
conditions: if lead agency coordination is assigned to the S/D Coordinator’s Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Receive suspension or debarment information from the ISDC through the OCP and disseminate to contracting officers and Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel; and
policy_statements.target: contracting officers and Mission Area, agency, and staff office S/D personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Send the Procurement SAM Memorandum (see Appendix F) to the OCP accompanied by the Notice of Suspension, Debarment, Disqualification or Voluntary Exclusion signed by the SDO.

The SAM Memorandum should be sent to OCP after respondent(s) notification(s) about suspension, debarment, and disqualification decisions, or following the receipt of an administrative agreement or settlement agreement between the respondent and the SDO that includes a voluntary exclusion.
(See FAR Subpart 9.4.)
Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Personnel will:

In coordination with the OIG, where applicable, will review and confirm potential causes for suspension or debarment actions obtained from external sources (e.g., OIG, other Federal agencies, hotline complaints, media) or through internal operations (e.g., review of contractor performance), and report findings to the S/D Council Member and contracting officer; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Personnel
policy_statements.target: potential causes for suspension or debarment actions

policy_statements.source_text: Assist the contracting officer in any Mission Area, agency, or staff office procurement S/D-related issues.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office S/D Personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Contracting Officers will:
Review exclusions in the GSA SAM Exclusions database after the opening of bids or receipt of proposals and immediately prior to award.
conditions: after the opening of bids or receipt of proposals and immediately prior to award
policy_statements.target: exclusions in the GSA SAM Exclusions database

policy_statements.source_text: Contractors listed in the GSA SAM Exclusions database will not receive awards and will have their bids or proposals rejected, unless the Agency Administrator decides otherwise in accordance with FAR 9.405-1(b) and AGAR 409.405-1;
policy_statements.actor_name: Contractors listed in the GSA SAM Exclusions database
conditions: unless the Agency Administrator decides otherwise in accordance with FAR 9.405-1(b) and AGAR 409.405-1

policy_statements.source_text: Refer contractors that may not be presently responsible to the S/D Coordinator for lead agency coordination, where appropriate; and
policy_statements.target: contractors that may not be presently responsible

policy_statements.source_text: When recommending that the SDO initiate suspension or debarment actions, prepare the Procurement Referral Record and Referral Memorandum (see Appendix G), to establish an Administrative Record in consultation with the S/D Council Member and the OGC if needed, and forward to the S/D Coordinator.
conditions: When recommending that the SDO initiate suspension or debarment actions
policy_statements.target: Procurement Referral Record and Referral Memorandum

policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
